title: Cross-Layer Reliability Evaluation and Efficient Hardening of Large Vision Transformers Models
problem: Measuring the error rate of large Vision Transformer models under hardware faults is prohibitively expensive, as conventional microarchitectural fault simulations require years to produce statistically significant results. ViTs are particularly vulnerable due to their large size and complexity.
motivation: Vision Transformers are increasingly deployed in critical applications, but their error rates under transient hardware faults have not been adequately characterized, creating reliability and safety risks.
method: The paper employs a two-level evaluation combining 70+ hours of neutron beam experiments with 600+ hours of software fault simulation across 12 ViT models on 2 NVIDIA GPU architectures. They characterize fault propagation in ViT kernels to identify critical faults likely to reach outputs. They propose MaxiMals (Maximum corrupted Malicious values), an experimentally tuned mitigation technique that efficiently detects and corrects corrupted values without significantly impacting performance.
key_novelty: MaxiMals is a low-cost runtime mitigation mechanism specifically tuned for ViT fault patterns that achieves 90.7% correction of critical failures with only 5.61% execution overhead.
contributions: Cross-layer fault evaluation framework combining physical neutron beam experiments and simulation
Characterization of fault propagation behavior in Vision Transformer kernels
MaxiMals mitigation technique for efficient detection and correction of transient faults
Demonstration of practical fault tolerance for large ViT models with minimal performance penalty
primary_theme: Fault-tolerant vision transformers via cross-layer evaluation
